findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation loop, blocking all later cancellations
findings.body: The cancellation loop awaits `client.request` for each cancelled reminder inside a single try block. If the request throws for one reminder (for example because SendGrid already sent that batch, or returns an error for a stale batch_id), the exception skips every remaining reminder and jumps to the catch that only logs. The failing reminder is not deleted or marked, so the next cron run (every 15 minutes) hits the same reminder first and fails again. Other cancelled reminders in the window are never cancelled at SendGrid and their emails still go out. Each reminder should be wrapped in its own try/catch so one failure does not block the rest.

findings.title: immediateDelete path cancels at SendGrid but leaves the workflowReminder row behind
findings.body: When `immediateDelete` is true and a referenceId exists, the function sends the SendGrid cancel and returns without touching the database. The workflowReminder row stays with scheduled=true and a now-cancelled referenceId. Callers that rely on this path (handleNewBooking for the original rescheduled booking, and workflows.tsx when deleting a workflow or step) leave orphaned rows behind. The other branches (no referenceId, SMS) do delete the row, so this behavior is inconsistent. The row should be deleted after a successful cancel, or the caller should be documented to handle cleanup.

findings.title: Cancellation window of one hour with a 15-minute cron can still let cancelled emails be sent
findings.body: A reminder is only picked up for SendGrid cancellation when its scheduledDate is within the next hour, and the cron runs every 15 minutes. If a booking is cancelled less than about 15 minutes before the reminder's sendAt, the next cron run may happen after sendAt, so SendGrid has already sent the email. The window is not guaranteed to contain a cron run before send time. The issue this PR fixes is exactly that cancelled reminders are still sent, so this residual gap should be addressed, for example by cancelling immediately when the reminder is close to its send time, or by using a shorter cron interval.

findings.title: No tests added for the new cancelled-flag flow and cron cancellation
findings.body: The PR changes the cancellation contract (cancelled flag set in deleteScheduledEmailReminder, deferred SendGrid cancel in the cron, immediate-delete variant, and DB row deletion in SMS and email paths). None of this is covered by tests. The cron's failure behavior, the cancelled-flag set/unset rules, and the reschedule and cancel paths in handleCancelBooking, handleNewBooking, and bookings.tsx all need coverage to prevent regressions like the one this PR is fixing.

findings.title: New nullable cancelled column has no default and no index for the cron query
findings.body: The column is added as nullable `BOOLEAN` with no default, so existing rows get NULL and the schema models it as `Boolean?`. The cron filters on `cancelled = true` and `scheduledDate <= ...` on every run, with no index on either column, so it scans the whole WorkflowReminder table each time. A default of false and a composite index on (cancelled, scheduledDate) would avoid this as the table grows.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation promises are fired without await inside forEach
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called inside `forEach` without awaiting. The handler then continues and responds while the cancelled-flag writes and Twilio cancels are still in flight. Errors are swallowed by the internal try/catch, so a failed cancel is silent. Using `Promise.all` with `map` would make the cancel complete before the response and keep the handler's ordering explicit. The same pattern appears in bookings.tsx and workflows.tsx.
